title: Truth because it's true (10:2)
hook: the one who serves from love does the truth because it is the truth
tomorrow: why does a law book quote a love song?

segments.voice: Yesterday: from love. Not for the reward, not out of fear; the week's six lines were heading there. Today, love gets a test with no audience.

Saturday afternoon, the checkout line. The cashier is rushing, the line is long, and she hands back change for a twenty when you paid with a ten. You notice in the parking lot. Nobody else will ever know. The store won't miss it tonight; the cashier might, at the end of her shift, counting a drawer that comes up short. Back inside, or into the car? And the more interesting question isn't which. It's why.
screen: `CHANGE FOR A TWENTY.` → `NOBODY WILL EVER KNOW.` → `NOT WHICH, BUT WHY.`

segments.voice: Maimonides answers the why. The one who serves from love, he writes, studies and keeps the commandments and walks in the paths of wisdom not for anything in this world: not for fear of bad things, not to inherit good things. They do the truth because it is the truth, and the good comes in the end anyway. Then he adds that this level is very great, and not every sage reaches it. It is the level of Abraham, whom God calls, in Isaiah, "the seed of Abraham my friend." In Hebrew, the word for my friend is ohavi: the one who loves me. Abraham, Maimonides says, served only from love. So, back to the parking lot. Go back in because you might get caught on camera: that's fear. Go back in because good things come to good people: that's reward. Go back in because the money isn't yours, that's true, and true is enough: that's the one he means. Here's the line worth repeating tonight: in this law book, honesty isn't a strategy. It's what love looks like when nobody's checking. And notice the small phrase at the end. The good comes in the end. He doesn't say love goes unrewarded. He says the reward stops being the reason.
screen: `NOT FOR FEAR, NOT FOR GAIN.` · `THE TRUTH, BECAUSE IT'S TRUE.` · `ABRAHAM: OHAVI, MY FRIEND.` · `THE GOOD COMES IN THE END.` · then, large: `TRUTH BECAUSE IT'S TRUE.`

segments.voice: Write one sentence on paper that is simply true about today: nothing clever, nothing you'd post. I was tired. I missed someone. The coffee was good. Read it back once, and sit with a true thing that has no audience until the bell.
Truth because it's true: Maimonides' mark of serving from love. The right thing, done because it's right.
Pocket this: truth because it's true; the reward stops being the reason. Twenty-five of thirty in the laws.

howItsDone: Jewish teachers point to Abraham, called God's friend in Isaiah 41:8, as the model of serving from love; honesty in business is a classic subject of Jewish law and ethics.

fork.setup: your group project gets an A. you spot a math mistake in your own chart that the teacher missed. what's the 'from love' move?
options: tell the teacher, because the chart is wrong.
tell the teacher, so it can't be held against you later.
fix it quietly next time; the grade is already in.
fork.reveal: the second option does the right act for a fear reason. the first does the truth because it's true, which is the level Maimonides calls love.
